verdict: real growth pattern, wrong model shape -- rate_rel suspect, not just DRIFT_FRAC
notes: Expanded the market-wide backfill from a 2-point (h1/h3) check to a full horizon ladder (lags 1-4 across jornadas 4/5/6, same 4 historical commits re-queried for more targets, canonical load_actuals()/lagged_pair() join). rate_rel-normalised Var(z) grows MONOTONICALLY with lag (20.3 -> 25.5 -> 62.2 -> 101.9 at n=113/88/59/19) -- a real, consistent pattern, not an outlier artifact. But fitting Var(lag) = intercept + slope*lag gives intercept=-17.8, when the model (rate_rel^2 * (1 + lag*DRIFT_FRAC^2)) requires intercept~=1.0 -- variance can't be negative, so the two-parameter DRIFT_FRAC model doesn't actually fit this population's shape. Reading: rate_rel itself is likely mis-scaled (too small) for the wider market -- probably thin-history/fringe players needing a different uncertainty floor -- not solely a DRIFT_FRAC question. Real next step: check ffcore.score._priors()/rate_rel's formula against realised variance for non-squad players specifically, before touching DRIFT_FRAC at all.

verdict: ruled out two candidate confounds, real mismatch remains unexplained
notes: Followed up the horizon-ladder finding (previous entry) with two controls, both ruling themselves out rather than fixing anything: (1) grid-searched the variance-side pseudo-count replacing SHRINK_MATCHES=8.0's reuse for rate_rel -- every candidate from 0.5 to 20 gives an impossible negative regression intercept, smaller values make it WORSE not better, so this isn't a SHRINK_MATCHES mistuning; (2) suspected the backfill's algebraic n= (cv/rel)^2-SHRINK_MATCHES used TODAY's cv (0.993) to reinterpret predictions made under each historical commit's OWN, different cv (0.97-1.07 across the 4 commits, real match pool 64->885 as the season played out) -- refetched each commit's actual fc._cv directly and reran: intercept barely moved (-15.2 vs -17.8). The monotonic variance growth with lag is real and now survives 3 independent checks; what generates it is NOT the simple rate_rel^2*(1+lag*DRIFT_FRAC^2) shape the model assumes. Genuinely unresolved -- likely needs a different functional form (e.g. news/injury information arriving nonlinearly as kickoff approaches, not a flat per-jornada random walk) rather than another parameter tune. Stopping here rather than continuing to grid-search blind.

verdict: DRIFT_FRAC signal was an artifact; real finding is rate_rel's absolute scale
notes:
SUPERSEDES the last 3 entries. Bootstrap.expected(T) returns the UNCONDITIONAL E[pts]=pts*p_start, but actuals (load_actuals(), games_delta>=1) are conditional on having played -- comparing them mixes P(start) miscalibration into what looked like RATE drift, worse at longer lags because P(start) predictions further out are less accurate. Redid the same horizon ladder using the CONDITIONAL prediction (pts alone, from per_jornada) instead: variance goes FLAT across lags (19.3/16.4/17.0/13.5 at n=113/88/59/19) and mean signed log-error collapses to ~0 at every lag (was 0.22->0.82, monotonically drifting). Regression slope on the corrected data is slightly negative -> DRIFT_FRAC has NO real evidence to move from 1.0 in this data; the 4.58/1.33 estimates in the prior 3 entries were measuring the P(start) artifact, not rate drift.
Separately: pooled conditional Var(z)=17.65 (n=279) is still far above the theoretical ~1-2 -- rate_rel itself needs to be ~3-4x bigger to match this. This does NOT contradict forecast.md's own squad-log measurement (Var~0.17-0.20 at h1) -- that method uses an EMPIRICALLY-FIT pooled rel (pstdev of actual/predicted ratios, self-normalizing h1 near-tautologically), while this test used the model's own THEORETICAL Bootstrap.rate_rel (cv/sqrt(n+SHRINK_MATCHES)) -- a genuinely independent check the squad-log method structurally cannot do (it can only compare h3 to whatever h1 turned out to be, never check if the absolute base level is right). Stratifying by backed-out n found the shortfall is LARGER for high-evidence players (needed_alpha 2.4/4.4/5.2 across n terciles), the opposite of what a SHRINK_MATCHES-too-generous-for-thin-history theory would predict -- points at cv/the 1/sqrt(n) shrinkage SHAPE itself understating a real week-to-week variance floor that doesn't shrink arbitrarily with more history, not at a specific pseudo-count constant. Real next step: check whether rate_rel needs a variance FLOOR (a minimum irreducible week-to-week uncertainty independent of n), not a bigger pseudo-count or a DRIFT_FRAC change.

verdict: confirmed: rate_rel needs a floor (~0.5), not a scale or pseudo-count change
notes: Direct test of the two candidate mechanisms for the conditional-corrected ~3-4x rate_rel shortfall found in drift_frac_conditional_fix: a flat multiplicative scale (scale*rel) vs a minimum floor (max(floor, rel)). Both can hit the pooled Var(z)~2 target with one free parameter (scale~3.0 or floor~0.50) -- that alone proves nothing. The real test: does either explain the n-tercile pattern (high-n players needing MORE correction, found earlier)? Floor=0.50 equalizes all three n-terciles into a tight, plausible range (Var=1.69/1.92/2.36 for low/mid/high n) -- a flat scale=3.0 leaves them wildly split (0.64/2.13/3.03, ~5x spread) because it can't discriminate between players whose rate_rel was already small (high n) vs already large (low n). CONCLUSION: rate_rel needs a MINIMUM FLOOR representing irreducible week-to-week uncertainty (fitness, matchup, tactical role) that does not shrink to zero no matter how much history a player has -- the current 1/sqrt(n+SHRINK_MATCHES) shape has no such floor and over-shrinks established players' uncertainty. Real, concrete next step if picked up: add a floor parameter to Bootstrap.rate_rel (ffcore/forecast.py), fit it walk-forward the way HOME_EDGE/_fit_decay() are fit, same out-of-sample discipline -- n=279 from a 4-commit backfill is real signal but should be reconfirmed as the market-wide squad_log logging (report.py, shipped 2026-09-16) accumulates clean, non-reconstructed history.
